entries.core_move: Convert between $e^{j\theta}$ and $\cos\theta + j\sin\theta$ using Euler’s formula to connect complex exponential form with sinusoidal real and imaginary parts in continuous-time signals.

Represent a complex signal quantity as $a + jb$ by separating its real and imaginary parts and interpreting them as rectangular coordinates for later polar, phasor, and complex-exponential signal analysis.
Convert a complex number from rectangular form into polar magnitude-phase form by computing its modulus and quadrant-correct angle for use in complex exponential and phasor representations.

Interpret $e^{j\omega t}$ as a unit-magnitude complex number rotating in the complex plane at angular frequency $\omega$, connecting Euler’s formula and polar form to sinusoidal phasor and Fourier representations.

entries.lesson_title: Real and Imaginary Parts of Complex Exponentials
entries.core_move: Extract the cosine and sine signal components from complex exponentials by applying Euler’s formula to identify their real and imaginary parts for later phasor and sinusoid representations.

entries.lesson_title: Magnitude and Phase of a Complex Exponential
entries.core_move: Compute the magnitude and phase of $C e^{j\omega t}$ by reading $|C|$ as the constant amplitude and $\angle C + \omega t$ as the time-varying angle that links complex-exponential form to rotating phasors and sinusoidal components.
